WITH patient_stats AS (
  SELECT p.ID AS ID, p.SEX AS sex, AVG(l.WBC) AS avg_wbc, AVG(l.HGB) AS avg_hgb, AVG(l.HCT) AS avg_hct
  FROM Laboratory l
  JOIN Patient p ON l.ID = p.ID
  GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX
),
ratios AS (
  SELECT ID, sex, avg_wbc, avg_hgb / avg_hct AS ratio
  FROM patient_stats
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(ratio) AS mean_ratio FROM ratios
)
SELECT r.ID, r.sex, r.avg_wbc, r.ratio, r.ratio - o.mean_ratio AS diff
FROM ratios r
CROSS JOIN overall o
WHERE r.ratio > o.mean_ratio
ORDER BY diff IS NULL, diff DESC
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: The database is SQLite, since the schema uses backtick-quoted identifiers and the query relies on CTEs, AVG, and LIMIT.
The ratio is the average HGB divided by the average HCT per patient (ratio of averages, not the average of per-row ratios), and it is NULL when either average is NULL or HCT averages to zero.
Average WBC, HGB, and HCT are computed over all of a patient's laboratory rows, with NULL values skipped by AVG; patients with no laboratory rows are dropped by the inner join.
The overall mean is taken over all patients whose ratio is non-NULL, and only patients with a non-NULL ratio strictly above that mean are listed.
Grouping by SEX uses Patient.SEX, and because Patient.ID is the primary key each patient appears as exactly one group.
